title_home: Pelusa – clean up your photo gallery and free up storage
desc_home: Scroll your photos as a feed and drop what you don’t need into containers. Free up space while your photos stay on your phone. Free, no ads.
og_desc: Scroll your photos as a feed and free up space. Free, no ads, photos never leave your phone.
pill: Free · No ads · Photos never leave your phone
h1: Scroll through memories. Free up memory.
sub: A feed as gripping as any other, but made of your photos and actually useful. Drop screenshots, blurry photos and duplicates into containers, then delete them to free up space.
soon_t: Coming soon to the App Store and Google Play
soon_p: Pelusa is almost ready: I’m finishing the last details before launch.
qr: Scan with your phone’s camera to open the right store
c1: 20 minutes of scrolling the feed – nothing changed.
c2b: of free space and a pleasant dose of nostalgia.
c2_nogb: 20 minutes of Pelusa – free space on your phone and a pleasant dose of nostalgia.
how_t: Three steps to free up space
s1_p: Hold a photo you don’t need, then tap others. They gather into a stack.
s2_t: Drop the stack in a container
s2_p: Drag the stack into the jar, the box or the bucket. Or just tap the container you want.
s3_p: Open a container, mark what to keep and tap “Delete the rest”. You can usually restore deleted photos for 30 days.
nos_p: Pick “Oldest first” in Sort and scroll back through the years. To keep new photos out of the way, use “Show photos” in Settings.
snd_t: You hear it and feel it in your hand
snd_p: Each container has its own sound. The jar rings, the box thuds, the bag rustles, and your phone gives a soft tap in your palm. The sounds are real recordings, no AI. Just a pantry, containers and beans.
snd_c1: Its own sound for each container
snd_c2: A soft tap in your hand
pad_note: You start with three. Add more any time, including a bag and a tub.
res_t: See how much space you freed
res_p: After each deletion, Pelusa shows how much space you freed up and celebrates with you. Stats add it all up by week.
trash: You can usually restore deleted photos for 30 days. After that, they’re erased permanently.
tr_android: Android: deleted photos go to your phone’s trash. Restore them right in Pelusa, on the Trash screen.
tr_ios: iPhone: deleted photos go to Recently Deleted in the Photos app and stay there for 30 days. Pelusa keeps a history of what was deleted, with a button that opens Photos.
st3: Nothing is deleted until you confirm
prv_c1: On iPhone and Android 14+ you can grant access to selected photos only
prv1_t: Your photos stay on your phone
prv1_p: Pelusa shows photos right from your gallery and never sends them anywhere, not to us, not to anyone.
prv2_p: Photos are deleted only after you confirm in the phone’s system dialog. And even then you can usually restore them.
prv3_p: When “Help make Pelusa better” is on, Pelusa sends crash reports and usage stats to Firebase by Google, never your photos, name or advertising ID. In the EU, it’s off until you turn it on.
ab_t: Made with love for my wife ❤️
ab_p1: Hi, I’m Sergei, a developer from Buenos Aires. Pelusa started as a gift for my wife: I wanted her to spend her evenings scrolling through our memories instead of strangers’ stories, with no screenshots or receipts in the way.
ab_p2: I build Pelusa on my own, in the evenings.
fr_p1: No ads, no subscriptions. Every feature is free.
fr_p2: If Pelusa made your evening a little cozier, you can support the author with a one-time purchase, like leaving a tip at your favorite café. In return, a “Pelusa supporter” badge appears in Settings. Any amount unlocks all supporter extras, including future ones.
q0: Why does Pelusa need access to my photos?
a0: To show your gallery as a feed. Pelusa shows photos right from your gallery and never sends them anywhere. On iPhone and Android 14+ you can allow access to selected photos only, and Pelusa will work with those. Nothing is deleted until you confirm in your phone’s system dialog.
q1: Does Pelusa delete photos on its own?
a1: No. Photos are deleted only after you confirm in the phone’s system dialog. And even then you can restore them for 30 days. On rare Android phones without a trash, deleting is permanent right away. Pelusa tells you about it after deleting.
q2: How do I restore deleted photos?
a2: On Android, right in Pelusa, on the Trash screen. On iPhone, in Recently Deleted in the Photos app, where photos are kept for 30 days.
q3: Will a photo be deleted from iCloud or Google Photos?
a3_1: iPhone: if iCloud Photos is on, deleting removes the photo from all your devices and from iCloud. This is how iPhone works. After 30 days, the photo is deleted permanently.
a3_2: Android: Pelusa deletes photos only from the phone. A copy in Google Photos, if there is one, stays.
q4: Do I need an internet connection?
a4: No, Pelusa works offline. Try it in airplane mode. The network is only used for crash reports and stats (you can turn them off in Settings) and for support purchases. On iPhone with iCloud Photos, the system may download a photo from iCloud when you open it full screen.
q5: Will Pelusa find duplicates and bad photos for me?
a5: No, and that’s on purpose. No AI decides for you what matters. You just scroll, remember and drop what you don’t need into a container.
a6: Whatever you like. Containers have no labels: screenshots go in the jar, receipts in the box, “I’ll sort it later” in the bucket. Each one sounds different, so they’re easy to tell apart.
a7: I made Pelusa for my family, and I’d like it to help others too. There are no ads or subscriptions. If you’d like to say thanks, you can support the author in Settings.
final: A minute with old photos, and more space on your phone
